title: agent-atlas External System manifest
description: An external system or datastore an agent/tool connects to: a database, vector store, graph/ontology store, FHIR endpoint, or third-party API. Lets the model answer 'what touches this datastore?'.

systemKind.description: The class of system. 'System' is the umbrella for anything acted upon (not an actor): DATA sources (relational-db/vector-store/graph-db/document-store/fhir/state-store — governed by classification/residency/retention), SERVICES (external-api/service — a write/egress target governed by scoped auth), and COMPUTE (compute-resource e.g. a GPU pool — governed by quota/priority/contention via resource-admission, NOT the proof spine). Governance metadata that matters DIFFERS by subtype (a planned discriminated-union refinement); see object-semantics.md.

governance.description: Regime-neutral trust/privacy controls (NIST AI RMF: privacy, security, accountability). The control is declared here; which standard it satisfies is named by data_tags and the model-level compliance_regimes. Optional — declare what the requirements state; leave the rest for a human.

data_classification.description: Sensitivity of the data this object touches.

data_tags.description: Regulatory data classes (MULTIPLE may apply, e.g. PHI and PII).

residency.description: Where data may be processed/stored. 'on-prem' = never leaves the boundary.

redaction.description: Fields to filter/redact/drop before telemetry is indexed (so observability isn't a compliance liability).
